newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney denies allegations in Espy lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney denies allegations in Espy lawsuit.

text.p: Smith Barney, a unit of Travelers Group, on Tuesday denied allegations that it tried to help a client by giving a Super Bowl ticket to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.
The company said it agreed to pay a $1.05 million settlement to the independent counsel investigating Espy to "settle the matter to avoid costly and protracted litigation."

"The firm acknowledges that its employee purchased the Super Bowl ticket for the outside consultant, along with two other tickets, but Smith Barney management was not aware of the purchase of the ticket because the employee submitted an invoice containing an inaccurate description of the expense," the company said in a statement.
The employee has been placed on administrative leave, Smith Barney said.
"The firm specifically denies that it or its employee gave a gratuity to Secretary Espy," the statement said.

Special prosecutor Donald Smaltz has been investigating Espy for the past three years over allegations that the former Clinton Administration cabinet member accepted gifts and favors from companies he regulated.
